samples.text:
The maps show how the village of Ashfield has changed from 1995 until now. Overall, the village become more developed and all the farmland was replaced by buildings.

In 1995, there was a river in the north and a main road from west to east. There was a church in the centre and two group of houses in the west. Also, there was farmland in the north-east and a big area of farmland in the south-west. A village shop was in the south of the road and there were a lot of trees in the south-east.

Nowadays, the farmland in the south-west has been changed to three housing estates and a new road called Ash Lane was built between them. In the north-east, the farmland was replaced by a primary school and a playing field. The village shop is not there anymore and a supermarket with a car park have been built in same area. Also, the trees in the south-east are much less than before. The footpath became a cycle path but part of it is gone. The river, church and old houses did not change.
samples.why: Overview present but basic · main changes covered with some mechanical listing · repetitive linking (Also) · adequate vocabulary · several errors in tense, plurals, agreement and articles that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The two maps illustrate the transformation of Ashfield between 1995 and the present day. Overall, the village has become far more urbanised, with almost all of its farmland giving way to housing and community facilities, while the river, the main road and the historic centre have remained intact.

The most dramatic change has taken place in the south-west. The large expanse of farmland that once lay south of Main Road has been replaced by three housing estates, which are now served by a new road, Ash Lane, running southwards from the main road between them. Similarly, the farmland in the north-east, between the road and the River Ash, has made way to a primary school and, further east, a playing field.

To the south of the main road, the small village shop has been demolished and a larger supermarket, with an adjoining car park to its east, now stands in its place. Moreover, the woodland in the south-east has shrunk to a small cluster in the corner. The footpath has also been converted into a cycle path, although its middle section, beside the supermarket, has disappeared. Meanwhile, the church and the two blocks of houses in the west has not changed.
samples.why: Clear overview of main changes · key features logically grouped by area · good range of linking · some less common vocabulary (urbanised, made way) · mostly accurate with a couple of minor slips.

samples.text:
The maps compare the village of Ashfield in 1995 with its current layout. The most striking development is that the countryside surrounding the village core has been almost entirely built over, turning a rural settlement into a larger residential community with modern amenities, although its basic framework of river, road and church is unchanged.

In 1995, Ashfield consisted of little more than a church and two blocks of houses on the northern side of Main Road, which crossed the village from west to east, with the River Ash flowing along its northern edge. Farmland occupied the north-east and a far larger area to the south-west, a village shop sat just south of the road, and a footpath led southwards, with extensive woodland to its east.

Today, the south-western fields have given way to three housing estates, divided by a newly built road, Ash Lane. In the north-east, a primary school and a playing field now occupy the former farmland. South of Main Road, the shop has been replaced by a considerably larger supermarket with a car park beside it, while the trees have been reduced to a small cluster in the south-eastern corner. Finally, the footpath has been converted into a cycle path, though the section alongside the supermarket no longer exists.
samples.why: Well-placed overview capturing the shift from rural to residential · changes skilfully selected and located precisely · seamless cohesion · precise, natural vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
